meta.notes: Non-ball consumables and materials only. Capture balls are a separate collection and are excluded here. Fusion items (Pitaya, Evofossils, Evodisks, Evostatues, Ancestral Blade, etc.) and equipment materials (Enhance Stone, Refine Stone) are out of scope for this consumables-and-materials collection. Food items and Tools (Shovel, XPNATOR) come from the authoritative EvoMon Wiki (wiki.gg) Items page with exact effect wording. EXP Fruit sizes, the reroll potions, and the evolution stones are not listed on the wiki.gg Items page; their existence and effects are corroborated across Pro Game Guides, Sportskeeda, and Nerdschalk. SOURCE CAUTION: evomon-world.wiki is an AI-embellished source that fabricates items/tiers; it was NOT used as a sole source for any row. Its claim that only four element stones (Fire/Water/Leaf/Thunder) exist is contradicted by reliable sources, which describe a large Pokemon-style element set. Element Stones are therefore modeled as a single family row rather than per-element rows to avoid inventing an unverified roster. Effect wording is paraphrased in our own words, not copied verbatim from sources. No active code names, dates, or freshness claims are stored.

items.name: EXP Fruit (Small)
items.cardSummary: The entry-tier EXP fruit, fed to an Evomon for a small amount of experience without battling.
items.effect: Grants a small amount of EXP
items.howToGet: Earned from battles, quests, daily play, and redeemed codes.
items.sourceStatus: Existence and EXP tiering corroborated by Pro Game Guides; effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: EXP Fruit sizes are not catalogued with an icon on the EvoMon Wiki (wiki.gg) Items page; no clean per-item sprite found.

items.name: EXP Fruit (Medium)
items.cardSummary: A mid-tier EXP fruit that gives more experience than the Small fruit, handy for leveling without grinding.
items.effect: Grants a moderate amount of EXP
items.howToGet: Earned from battles, quests, daily play, and redeemed codes.
items.sourceStatus: Corroborated by Pro Game Guides (codes reward and farming guide); effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: EXP Fruit sizes are not catalogued with an icon on the EvoMon Wiki (wiki.gg) Items page; no clean per-item sprite found.

items.name: EXP Fruit (Large)
items.cardSummary: The highest-tier EXP fruit, giving the most experience per fruit for fast leveling.
items.effect: Grants a large amount of EXP
items.howToGet: Earned from EXP Dungeons, weekly quests, beating or releasing Evomon, and redeemed codes.
items.sourceStatus: Corroborated by Pro Game Guides farming guide; effect paraphrased

items.name: Talent Vector Potion
items.cardSummary: Rerolls a captured Evomon's Talent, shuffling its boosted stats without changing the talent rank itself.
items.howToGet: Earned from the Season Battle Pass, Tower Ascent floor rewards, and redeemed codes.
items.sourceStatus: Confirmed as a real item by Sportskeeda Battle Pass and Tower Ascent guides; effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: reroll potions are not catalogued with an icon on wiki.gg; no clean per-item sprite found.

items.name: Trait Reroll Potion
items.cardSummary: Changes the Trait of a captured Evomon to a different randomly rolled trait.
items.howToGet: Earned from the Season Battle Pass and redeemed codes.
items.sourceStatus: Confirmed as a real item by Sportskeeda Battle Pass guide; effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: reroll potions are not catalogued with an icon on wiki.gg; no clean per-item sprite found.

items.name: Nature Reroll Potion
items.cardSummary: Changes the Nature of a captured Evomon, the third reroll potion alongside the Talent and Trait potions.
items.howToGet: Earned from the Season Battle Pass and redeemed codes.
items.sourceStatus: Confirmed as a real item by Sportskeeda Battle Pass guide; effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: reroll potions are not catalogued with an icon on wiki.gg; no clean per-item sprite found.

items.name: Evolution Stone
items.cardSummary: The universal evolution material every Evomon needs, spent alongside the matching Element Stones at a level milestone.
items.howToGet: Buy from the Exchange Merchant (5 stones for 10 Exchange Tokens, weekly refresh), earn from island and Summon Ruins bosses, player level-up rewards, and Battle Pass rewards.
items.sourceStatus: Confirmed distinct universal item by Sportskeeda, Nerdschalk, and Pro Game Guides; effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: the generic Evolution Stone is not catalogued with an icon on wiki.gg; only fusion evofossil sprites exist, which are a different item.

items.name: Element Stones
items.cardSummary: Type-locked stones that match an Evomon's element, spent with Evolution Stones to evolve. Each element has its own stone, such as the Fire, Water, Grass, and Electric stones.
items.howToGet: First-time wins against NPC Trainers (one-time, area-themed), island and Summon Ruins bosses, and regional bosses matching the element.
items.sourceStatus: Confirmed by Sportskeeda and Nerdschalk; modeled as one family row because reliable sources list a large element set rather than four; effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: no clean representative element-stone icon catalogued on wiki.gg; family row stays text-first.

items.name: Omni Stone
items.cardSummary: A flexible substitute that fills in for any missing Element Stone during an evolution, with one Omni Stone counting as one Element Stone.
items.howToGet: Buy from the Exchange Merchant and Traveling Merchant, earn from Tower rewards, and claim from Battle Pass rewards.
items.sourceStatus: Confirmed by Sportskeeda and Nerdschalk; effect paraphrased
items.imageStatus: accepted-missing: Omni Stone is not catalogued with an icon on wiki.gg; no clean per-item sprite found.
